---
title: "Bonus: finding stores with STAC"
subtitle: "Search the ocean-icechunks stores by place and time"
---

## Which stores cover my place and period?

If we have time and interest. The ocean-icechunks account holds many stores.
To pick the right ones, describe each store in a **catalog** you can search.

- **[STAC](https://stacspec.org)** is a standard format for catalogs of geospatial data. One
  **item** describes one store: where it is, when it covers, and what it holds
- **stac-geoparquet** keeps all the items in a single file
- **rustac** searches that file by place and time
- **xpystac** opens a match in xarray

::: notes
Bonus material, for the end of the day or for people who finish early. Nothing
here is needed for the rest of the tutorial.
:::

## A STAC item describes one store {.code}

```json
{
  "id": "pacioos-roms_hiig",
  "bbox": [-163.83, 17.02, -152.52, 23.98],
  "properties": {
    "start_datetime": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end_datetime": "2026-11-22T00:00:00Z",
    "storage:schemes": { "source-coop": { "anonymous": true, ... } }
  },
  "assets": { "data": {
    "href": "s3://.../ocean-icechunks/pacioos/roms_hiig/icechunk",
    "type": "application/vnd.zarr+icechunk",
    "storage:refs": ["source-coop"],
    "cube:variables": { "temp": ..., "salt": ..., ... } } }
}
```

::: notes
Trimmed from a real item: the bucket host, the UTC offsets and some fields are shortened. The bounding box and the time range are what the
search uses. The storage fields (the STAC storage extension) are what xpystac
reads to open the asset: the bucket, the region, and that no credentials are
needed. The asset type application/vnd.zarr+icechunk tells xpystac it is an
Icechunk store.
:::

## Build the catalog {.code}

```python
stores = list(find_stores("ocean-icechunks/"))   # walk the bucket listing
items = [make_item(path) for path in stores]     # read each store's metadata
await rustac.write("ocean-icechunks-items.parquet", items)
```

::: notes
find_stores and make_item are defined step by step in the notebook
stac-geoparquet-create. It lists the public bucket, opens each Icechunk store
and reads only the small coordinate arrays, never the data, then writes one
item per store: 8 items on 2026-11-17. It takes about a minute. Nothing is
stored in the repository: everyone builds the catalog themselves.

The three noaa-ohc stores each keep several datasets in groups (14day,
14day_v1, daily). Those become several assets on one item.
:::

## Search it, then open a match {.code}

```python
hits = await rustac.search("ocean-icechunks-items.parquet",
                           bbox=[-158.5, 20.5, -157.5, 21.5],  # Oahu
                           datetime="2026-01-01/2026-02-01")   # 3 of 8 stores match
item = pystac.Item.from_dict(next(h for h in hits if h["id"] == "pacioos-roms_hiig"))
ds = xr.open_dataset(item.assets["data"], engine="stac")
```

::: notes
Run on 2026-11-17: the search returns noaa-ohc-np, pacioos-roms_hiig and
pacioos-ww3_hawaii, and roms_hiig opens with 6 variables. The reanalyses ended
before 2026, and the other ocean heat content basins do not cover Hawaii.

xpystac always opens the root of a store, so it cannot open the noaa-ohc
groups. The notebook opens those by hand with icechunk and xr.open_zarr. It
needs an xpystac newer than release 0.5.0. Check that the workshop image has
one before presenting this.
:::
